reading: Every isolated marker (colour 1) gets a 3x3 badge: centre 2, orthogonal neighbours 1, diagonal neighbours 3; then a full row and full column of colour 1 run through the marker to the borders, painting only background (they pass under other badges).
why: unit = [313/121/313] centred on each marker; lines of colour 1 go in all four directions from each 2-cell to the border and overwrite only background cells (badges drawn after lines would give the same result).
invariants: line colour 1, badge colours 2 and 3 are constant

reading: The yellow (4) cells are pieces of plus shapes (centre + 4 arms, clipped at the border); each plus whose cells are all non-zero is completed by turning its grey (5) cells red (2).

new_rows.name: plus5
new_rows.datalog:
arm(DY, DX) :- off(DY, DX), DY = 0.
arm(DY, DX) :- off(DY, DX), DX = 0.
inx(Y, X, Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C).
inx(Y, X, Y2, X2) :- px(Y, X, C), arm(DY, DX), Y2 = Y + DY, X2 = X + DX, px(Y2, X2, C2).
holed(Y, X) :- inx(Y, X, Y2, X2), px(Y2, X2, 0).
n4(Y, X, count(Y2, X2)) :- inx(Y, X, Y2, X2), px(Y2, X2, 4).
cand(Y, X, N) :- n4(Y, X, N), N >= 2, !holed(Y, X).
beaten(Y, X) :- cand(Y, X, N), inx(Y, X, Y2, X2), px(Y2, X2, 4), inx(Y3, X3, Y2, X2), cand(Y3, X3, M), M > N.
sel(Y, X) :- cand(Y, X, N), !beaten(Y, X).
plus5(Y2, X2) :- sel(Y, X), inx(Y, X, Y2, X2), px(Y2, X2, 5).

why: key 5->2; a plus is chosen if it has no 0 cell, holds >=2 yellow cells, and no other such plus with more yellow cells shares one of its yellow cells; chosen pluses cover every yellow cell exactly once. Colours are named explicitly because 5 outnumbers 0 in the test grid.
invariants: grey cells outside chosen pluses unchanged

reading: Every square object (box height = width > 1, all four box corners filled: square rings and solid squares) gets a red (2) tick on the background just outside each corner, one above/below and one left/right; non-square objects get nothing.

new_rows.name: tick
new_rows.datalog:
ominy(O, min(Y)) :- obj(O, Y, X).
omaxy(O, max(Y)) :- obj(O, Y, X).
ominx(O, min(X)) :- obj(O, Y, X).
omaxx(O, max(X)) :- obj(O, Y, X).
sq(O, Y0, Y1, X0, X1) :- ominy(O, Y0), omaxy(O, Y1), ominx(O, X0), omaxx(O, X1), H = Y1 - Y0, V = X1 - X0, H = V, H > 0, obj(O, Y0, X0), obj(O, Y0, X1), obj(O, Y1, X0), obj(O, Y1, X1).
tick(Y, X) :- sq(O, Y0, Y1, X0, X1), Y = Y0 - 1, X = X0, px(Y, X, C).
tick(Y, X) :- sq(O, Y0, Y1, X0, X1), Y = Y0, X = X0 - 1, px(Y, X, C).
tick(Y, X) :- sq(O, Y0, Y1, X0, X1), Y = Y0 - 1, X = X1, px(Y, X, C).
tick(Y, X) :- sq(O, Y0, Y1, X0, X1), Y = Y0, X = X1 + 1, px(Y, X, C).
tick(Y, X) :- sq(O, Y0, Y1, X0, X1), Y = Y1 + 1, X = X0, px(Y, X, C).
tick(Y, X) :- sq(O, Y0, Y1, X0, X1), Y = Y1, X = X0 - 1, px(Y, X, C).
tick(Y, X) :- sq(O, Y0, Y1, X0, X1), Y = Y1 + 1, X = X1, px(Y, X, C).
tick(Y, X) :- sq(O, Y0, Y1, X0, X1), Y = Y1, X = X1 + 1, px(Y, X, C).

why: key 7->2 on the 8 tick cells of each square object; lines, the 2x4 block and the 2-cell diagonal (corners not all filled) are skipped.

reading: The single grey shape is cut into pieces that tile it exactly: 2x2 squares become 8 and straight 1x3 bars (horizontal or vertical) become 2.

slots.subject: the one grey (5) shape
slots.pieces: 2x2 square -> colour 8; straight 3-cell bar, either orientation -> colour 2
slots.constraint: pieces are disjoint and cover every grey cell; background unchanged

why: each grey cell lies in exactly one piece, every piece is a 2x2 square or a 1x3 bar.

reading: An 8x8 yellow-bordered box holds a 2x-scaled 3x3 picture of colour c; in every 3x3 panel (cut by the yellow separator lines) whose blue (1) cells contain that picture's mask, the masked cells turn c and other 1s stay.

slots.template: the 6x6 area inside the 4-bordered 8x8 box, read at 2x2 scale as a 3x3 mask of its one colour c
slots.panels: the 3x3 cell blocks between the separator lines (outside the template box)
slots.action: if every mask cell is 1 in the panel, those cells become c

why: exact on all four pairs: only panels containing the full mask change, and only on mask cells.
invariants: 1 cells off the mask or in non-matching panels

reading: Each closed one-wide outline has its corner cells recoloured: convex corners (the diagonal between the two arms is inside the shape) become 4, concave corners (that diagonal is outside) become 2.

new_rows.name: convex
new_rows.datalog:
bgc(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), !cell(Y, X, C).
fgc(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C).
my(max(Y)) :- px(Y, X, C).
mx(max(X)) :- px(Y, X, C).
vdir(DY) :- off(DY, DX), DX = 0.
hdir(DX) :- off(DY, DX), DY = 0.
step(DY, DX) :- off(DY, DX), DY = 0.
step(DY, DX) :- off(DY, DX), DX = 0.
outside(Y, X) :- bgc(Y, X), Y = 0.
outside(Y, X) :- bgc(Y, X), X = 0.
outside(Y, X) :- bgc(Y, X), my(M), Y = M.
outside(Y, X) :- bgc(Y, X), mx(M), X = M.
outside(Y2, X2) :- outside(Y, X), step(DY, DX), Y2 = Y + DY, X2 = X + DX, bgc(Y2, X2).
corner(Y, X, DY, DX) :- cell(Y, X, C), vdir(DY), hdir(DX), Y1 = Y + DY, X1 = X + DX, fgc(Y1, X), fgc(Y, X1), Y2 = Y - DY, X2 = X - DX, !fgc(Y2, X), !fgc(Y, X2).
convex(Y, X) :- corner(Y, X, DY, DX), Y1 = Y + DY, X1 = X + DX, !outside(Y1, X1).

new_rows.name: concave
new_rows.datalog:
bgc(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), !cell(Y, X, C).
fgc(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C).
my(max(Y)) :- px(Y, X, C).
mx(max(X)) :- px(Y, X, C).
vdir(DY) :- off(DY, DX), DX = 0.
hdir(DX) :- off(DY, DX), DY = 0.
step(DY, DX) :- off(DY, DX), DY = 0.
step(DY, DX) :- off(DY, DX), DX = 0.
outside(Y, X) :- bgc(Y, X), Y = 0.
outside(Y, X) :- bgc(Y, X), X = 0.
outside(Y, X) :- bgc(Y, X), my(M), Y = M.
outside(Y, X) :- bgc(Y, X), mx(M), X = M.
outside(Y2, X2) :- outside(Y, X), step(DY, DX), Y2 = Y + DY, X2 = X + DX, bgc(Y2, X2).
corner(Y, X, DY, DX) :- cell(Y, X, C), vdir(DY), hdir(DX), Y1 = Y + DY, X1 = X + DX, fgc(Y1, X), fgc(Y, X1), Y2 = Y - DY, X2 = X - DX, !fgc(Y2, X), !fgc(Y, X2).
concave(Y, X) :- corner(Y, X, DY, DX), Y1 = Y + DY, X1 = X + DX, outside(Y1, X1).

why: key shape colour->4 on convex corners, then shape colour->2 on concave corners (test colour 3 appears in training); a corner is a shape cell with exactly one vertical and one horizontal shape neighbour; outside = background reachable from the border.

reading: The 3x3 input has one uniform row or column; the 9x9 output places three copies of the input along that row-band or column-band, the rest is 0.
why: block (i,k) holds the input iff input row i is uniform (or block (k,j) iff column j is uniform); other blocks empty.

reading: The top and bottom rows are walls of two colours; every loose object slides straight up or down until it touches the wall of its own colour, keeping its shape.

new_rows.name: loose
new_rows.datalog:
wid(count(X)) :- px(Y, X, C), Y = 0.
rowc(Y, C, count(X)) :- cell(Y, X, C).
wall(Y) :- rowc(Y, C, N), wid(N).
loose(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C), !wall(Y).

why: each object ends adjacent to the same-coloured wall, column unchanged. Exact on pair 1; on pair 0 everything matches except the 3-cell 8-bar in the last column, which shows as 5 cells (rows 10-14) instead of 3 (rows 12-14), so pair 0 looks noisy or has a rule I can't see.

reading: In each column whose bottom cell is coloured, every coloured cell paints upward in its own colour until the next coloured cell above (the top one runs to the border); other columns stay unchanged.

new_rows.name: src
new_rows.datalog:
bot(max(Y)) :- px(Y, X, C).
based(X) :- bot(M), cell(M, X, C).
src(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C), based(X).

why: lines go upward only (direction up), each stopping just under the next non-background cell, or at the top border; source cells keep their colour.

reading: The 3x9 grid is three 3x3 blocks; each block's grey pattern names a colour and the block is filled solid with it: top row->6, ring->3, bottom row->1, anti-diagonal->9, centre dot->4.

slots.action: fill the whole block with the key colour

why: the same pattern always gives the same colour across all four pairs; every test pattern is in the key.
